text.ms:
1. (1) Kaedah-kaedah ini bolehlah dinamakan Kaedah-Kaedah Buruh

(Lesen Untuk Menggaji Pekerja Bukan Pemastautin) (Sabah) 2026.

 (2) Kaedah-Kaedah ini mula berkuat kuasa pada 15 Februari 2026.

Tafsiran

2. Dalam Kaedah-Kaedah ini, "pemegang lesen" ertinya orang yang dinamakan

dalam lesen sebagai pemegang lesen.

Permohonan lesen

4. (1) Apabila suatu lesen dikeluarkan, pemegang lesen hendaklah

memastikan—

(a) bahawa pekerja bukan pemastautin itu diambil kerja—

(i) dalam jawatan sebagaimana yang dinyatakan dalam lesen;

dan

(ii) di alamat tempat pekerjaan sebagaimana yang dinyatakan

dalam lesen;

(b) bahawa apa-apa maklumat yang dinyatakan dalam lesen itu tidak

boleh ditukar tanpa kebenaran bertulis terlebih dahulu daripada

Pengarah;

(c) bahawa pekerja bukan pemastautin itu tidak diambil bekerja oleh

mana-mana orang lain selain pemegang lesen itu;

(d) bahawa dalam hal keadaan pengurangan tenaga kerja, pekerja

bukan pemastautin itu hendaklah diberhentikan terlebih dahulu

sebelum pekerja tempatan;

(e) bahawa apa-apa perbelanjaan yang dibuat bagi kemasukan pekerja

bukan pemastautin yang dilesenkan itu hendaklah ditanggung oleh

pemegang lesen bermula dari negara atau Negeri asal sehingga ke

premis pekerjaan;

(f) bahawa lesen yang dikeluarkan di bawah Kaedah-Kaedah ini tidak

boleh dipindah milik dan hanya sah untuk penggajian pekerja

bukan pemastautin yang dilesenkan itu;

(g) bahawa dalam hal keadaan penghantaran pulang seseorang pekerja

bukan pemastautin ke negara atau Negeri asal—

(i) seksyen 96 dan 97 Ordinan hendaklah terpakai;

(ii) Pengarah hendaklah diberitahu dalam tempoh tiga puluh

hari sebelum penghantaran pulang; dan

(iii) pemegang lesen itu hendaklah menguruskan penghantaran

pulang pekerja bukan pemastautin;

(h) bahawa dalam hal keadaan penamatan penggajian pekerja bukan

pemastautin, Pengarah hendahklah diberitahu dalam tempoh

tiga puluh dari tarikh penamatan sebagaimana dalam Jadual Ketiga;

(i) bahawa tempoh lesen yang dinyatakan dalam lesen itu belum habis

tempoh;

(j) bahawa dalam hal keadaan pemegang lesen itu berhasrat untuk

terus menggaji seorang pekerja bukan pemastautin yang lesennya

akan habis tempoh, pemegang lesen itu bolehlah membuat

permohonan untuk menggaji pekerja bukan pemastautin di bawah

kaedah 3 dalam tempoh enam puluh hari sebelum habis tempoh

lesen itu;

(k) bahawa lesen yang dikeluarkan di bawah Kaedah-Kaedah ini

hendaklah disediakan untuk pemeriksaan oleh Pengarah

sebagaimana dan apabila dikehendaki; dan

(l) bahwa dalam hal keadaan lesen itu hilang, rosak atau tercemar,

pemegang lesen itu hendaklah serta-merta memohon kepada

Pengarah bagi suatu salinan baharu lesen itu.

Malaysia

4. Seseorang pekerja bukan pemastautin hendaklah memegang dokumen

LABOUR ORDINANCE OF SABAH

LABOUR (LICENCE TO EMPLOY NON-RESIDENT EMPLOYEE) (SABAH) RULES 2026

IN exercise of the powers conferred by paragraph 130O(2)(n) of the

Labour Ordinance of Sabah [Sabah Cap. 67], the Minister after consultation with

the State Authority makes the following rules:

Citation and commencement

1. (1) These rules may be cited as the Labour (Licence To Employ

Non-Resident Employee) (Sabah) Rules 2026.

(2) These Rules come into operation on 15 February 2026.

Interpretation

2. In these Rules, "licensee" means the person named in the licence as the holder of

the licence.

Application for licence

3. (1) An application by a person who intends to apply for a licence to employ

a non-resident employee shall be made according to the conditions of applications in the

First Schedule in writing or by electronic means to the Director by furnishing the

following particulars:

(a) name of applicant;

(b) identity card number or passport number of individual applicant, or

registration number if applicable;

(c) address of applicant;

(d) address of place of employment;

(e) name of non-resident employee;

(f) identity card number or passport number of non-resident

employee;

(g) gender of non-resident employee ;

(h) designation of non-resident employee;

(i) country or State of origin of non-resident employee;

(j) non-resident employee's academic qualifications, if academic

requirements are specified; and

(k) non-resident employee's working experience, if work experience

requirements are specified.

(2) The particulars under subrule (1) shall be furnished to the nearest office

of the Director having administrative jurisdiction for the area in which place of

employment is located.

(3) Upon considering the application for a licence made under subrule (1),

the Director may—

(a) approve the application and issue to the applicant a Licence To

Employ Non-Resident Employee in a form as prescribed in the

Second Schedule; or

(b) refuse the application in writing.

Conditions of licence

4. (1) Upon issuance of the licence, the licensee shall ensure—

(a) that the non-resident employee is employed—

(i) in the designation as specified in the licence; and

(ii) at the address of place of employment as specified in the

licence.

(b) that any information specified in the licence shall not be changed

without the prior written permission of the Director;

(c) that the non-resident employee is not employed by any other

person other than the licensee;

(d) that in the event of workforce reduction, the non-resident

employee shall be terminated before the resident employee;

(e) that all expenses for the recruitment of the

non-resident employee shall be borne by the licensee from his

country or State of origin to the employment premises;

(f) that the licence issued under these Rules are non-transferable and

shall only be valid for the employment of the licensed non-resident

employee;

(g) that in the event of repatriation of a non-resident employee to his

country or State of origin—

(i) sections 96 and 97 of the Ordinance shall apply;

(ii) the Director shall be informed within thirty days prior to

repatriation; and

(iii) he shall manage the repatriation of the non-resident

employee;

(h) that in the event of termination of employment of non-resident

employee, the Director shall be informed within thirty days from

the date of termination as stated in Third Schedule;

(i) that the duration of the licence as specified in the licence has not

expired;

(j) that in the event he intends to continue employing a non-resident

employee whose licence will expire, he may make an application to

employ such non-resident employee under rule 3 within sixty days

before the expiry of such licence;

(k) that the licence issued under these Rules shall be made available for

the inspection by the Director as and when required; and

(l) that in the event the licence is lost, damaged or defaced, he shall

immediately apply to the Director for a new copy of the licence.

FIRST SCHEDULE

[Subrule 3(1)]

CONDITIONS OF APPLICATION FOR LICENCE TO EMPLOY NON-RESIDENT EMPLOYEE

(1)

No.

(2)

Conditions of application

1. A non-resident employee shall have attained the age of eighteen years

2. An applicant has no conviction for any offence under any written law in force in

Malaysia

3. A non-resident employee has no conviction for any offence under any written law

in force in Malaysia

4. A non-resident employee shall carry a valid travel document
